newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks sweep to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks sweep to higher close.

text.p: Buoyed by a successful global bond launch, Argentine stocks pierced resistance and rallied Wednesday on the back of a surge in the heavyweight telephone sector, dealers said.
"Telephone stocks, which were lagging the market, suddenly sprang to life and swept up the rest, causing much better volume," said Jorge Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 1.7 percent to a close at a 12-week high of 570.50, stretching gains so far this week to 2.7 percent. The MerVal rose 10 percent in September.

Telecom and Telefonica shot up 4.2 percent and 4.0 percent, respectively, tracking their gains in ADRs, while two other leading stocks listed abroad, Banco de Galicia and Banco Frances, rose 4.0 percent and 2.4 percent, respectively.

"The buying spree in ADRs created a sense of euphoria," said Napoli. Gains were tempered, however, by oil giant YPF's flat finish on Wall Street, with dealers saying the bellwether stock is facing profit-taking after its bull run last month on strong international crude prices and a leadership shakeup.
Argentina's $1.0 billion global bond launch Wednesday helped offset a weak September tax report, dealers said.

"A close look at the fiscal data shows that while collection fell 0.2 percent (from September 1995) this does not necessarily reflect slower economic activity that month," said an analyst at an emerging markets investment bank.

"Overall the good news outweighs the bad: industrial production and sales indicators are strong and the government is receiving so many offers for financing at home and abroad, that the idea of a slightly higher fiscal revenue forecast is nothing to worry about," he added.
Argentina boosted its global bond issue by $250 million on strong demand Tuesday. The bond fetched 11 percent interest.
In the session the all-share index rose 1.8 percent, with risers bashing decliners 43 to 11 and 24 issues unchanged.
Floor volume picked up to a moderately healthy tally of 21.6 million pesos from 13.6 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover swelled to 128.2 million pesos from 84.6 million Tuesday.

Top main-tier performers were carmaker Sevel and petrochemical company Indupa, which soared 7.0 percent and 5.4 percent, respectively. The only losers were petrochemical firm Ipako and steelmaker Acindar, off 1.3 percent and 0.6 percent.
